courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas from approximately 1500 CE through the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History to 1877
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from its origins to 1877. Includes the European exploration, development of the American colonies and their institutions, the Revolution, major political, social and economic developments, geographical expansion, the Civil War, and Reconstruction. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History Since 1865
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from 1865 to present. Includes major political, social and economic developments since 1865, overseas expansion, the two world wars, the Cold War and the post-Cold War era. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Women in American History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the role of women and attitudes toward women in American society from colonial times to the present.

courses.title: African-American History I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of African Americans from their African origins to 1876.

courses.title: African-American History II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of black Americans from their African origins to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: Historical Archaeology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces both the methods and theories in historical archaeology as practiced in the United States and worldwide. Includes time and space, field survey, excavation, archival and laboratory research. Includes field trips to site excavations.

courses.title: Introduction to Historic Preservation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a foundation and introduction to historic preservation practices and issues in Virginia and the United States. Emphasizes legislation, policies, and methodologies that form our present national, state, and local preservation systems.

courses.title: Survey of Museum Practice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the role of the museum in society and traces the foundations upon which these public, cultural and educational institutions are built. Emphasizes the management and interpretation of historic properties and collections.

courses.title: Collections Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses the fundamentals of collections policy, deaccessioning, appraisal, and curatorial management.

courses.title: Interpreting Material Culture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys America's material culture and provides techniques to interpret artifacts.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: History of African Civilization
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines major social, economic, political and religious developments across the African continent from earliest times to the present. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Local History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the history of the local community and/or region.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital History
courses.contact_hours: 3 Credits. Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the methods, theories and practices of digital history.

courses.title: Introduction to Latin American History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of Latin American civilizations from the pre-Columbian era to the present

courses.title: History of Russia I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys history of Russia from earliest times to the present. Includes political, economic, multi-national, social, and cultural aspects of Russian and Soviet history. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of the Ancient World I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the history of the ancient world from the dawn of civilization in the Near East to the fall of Rome. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of Middle East Civilization I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys intellectual, cultural, social, economic and religious patterns in the civilizations of the Middle East. Covers Semitic, Indo-European, and Turkic-speaking peoples from pre-Islamic to the present. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of Modern East Asian Civilizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines East Asian civilizations from the early modern period through the present day.

courses.title: The Second World War
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines causes and consequences of the Second World War. Includes the rise of totalitarianism, American neutrality, military developments, the home fronts, diplomacy, and the decision to use the atomic bomb.

courses.title: Civil War and Reconstruction
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies factors that led to the division between the States. Examines the war, the home fronts, and the era of Reconstruction.

courses.title: United States History Since World War II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates United States history from 1945 to the present, studying both domestic developments and American involvement in international affairs.

courses.title: Age of the American Revolution
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the factors that led to the separation of the American colonies from Great Britain. The course covers the events leading to the Revolutionary War, the problems faced by the revolutionary government in fighting the war, the war itself, and the postwar events leading to the adoption of the United States Constitution.

courses.title: American Foreign Policy Since 1890
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines American foreign policy since 1890 with an emphasis on current events and diverse points of view.

courses.title: History of Virginia
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the cultural, economic, political, and religious history of Virginia from pre-contact to the present. Includes diverse perspectives to emphasize the significant contributions different groups of people (African Americans, Indigenous Peoples, European-Americans, Women) made to the history of Virginia, the colonies, and the United States.

courses.title: Introduction to Computers in Health Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Lab 3 hours per week. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: : Introduces students to computers in health care. Provides a basic overview of computer architecture, common software applications and their use in health care, electronic data management, adoption of the electronic health record (EHR), and privacy and security.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides training in coordinated mouth-to-mouth artificial ventilation and chest compression, choking, life-threatening emergencies, and sudden illness. Equivalent to EMS 100 .

courses.title: Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of health and dimensions of wellness through exploration of a variety of personal health topics. Identifies factors that affect the health status of individuals in addition to health promotion and disease prevention at the personal and community level.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on medical terminology for students preparing for careers in the health professions. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 143 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation and usage.

courses.title: Ethics for Health Care Personnel
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on ethical concepts of health care. Emphasizes confidentiality, maintaining patient records, personal appearance, professionalism with patients/clients, associates, and an awareness of health care facilities.

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the study of various forms of physical activity and how they promote human health. Examines the study of physical activity from the perspectives of professional practice, scholarly study and experience. Provides a broad overview of the history, scientific principles, methodologies, and research among the major subdisciplines to prepare students for further study in kinesiology and health sciences. Explores current issues, future directions, certifications, professional associations, and career opportunities.

courses.title: Concepts of Disease
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general principles, classifications, causes, and treatments of selected disease processes. Intended primarily for students enrolled in health technology programs.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of public health systems in the United States and globally with an emphasis on core functions, essential services and health determinants. Explores the history, core areas and current trends within public health as well as how public health affects individuals and populations. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of nutrition and its impact on personal wellness. Emphasizes an evidence-based approach to various topics, such as the nutrient components of food, the components of a healthy eating pattern, and the relationship between diet and health. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: Global Health Perspectives
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines global health theories, concepts, issues and prevention efforts. Analyzes the complex relationship between economics, environment, culture and values in addressing health disparities and access to healthcare around the globe. Explores health inequities across the globe by using contemporary, evidence-based topics.

courses.title: General Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general pharmacology for the health related professions covering general principles of drug actions/reactions, major drug classes, specific agent within each class, and routine mathematical calculations needed to determine desired dosages.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces human service agencies, roles and careers. Presents an historical perspective of the field as it relates to human services today. Additional topics include values clarification and needs of target populations.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills needed to function in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in attending, listening and responding. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement.

courses.title: Group Dynamics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the stages of group development, group dynamics, the role of the leader in a group, and recognition of the various types of group processes. Discusses models of group dynamics that occur as a result of group membership dynamics.

courses.title: Group Dynamics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines group dynamics, group leadership, group cohesion, transference and group helping through experiential involvement in group facilitating and leadership. Increases group skills through active classroom participation in group experiences.

courses.title: Effects of Psychoactive Drugs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides information on the biochemical, physiological, and behavioral aspects of substance addiction and will review the symptoms of addiction. Emphasizes areas of chemical dependency, medical epidemiology, physiological threats of addiction and methods of identifying multiple drug abusers.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides knowledge, skills, and insight for working in substance use programs. Emphasizes personal growth and client growth measures in helping relationships. Stresses various methods of individual and group techniques for helping the individual with substance use disorder.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: HMS 251 .
courses.description: Expands knowledge and skill in working with individuals with substance use disorder. Focuses on assisting people with substance use disorder in individual and group settings and explores client treatment modalities. May provide opportunities for field experience in treatment centers.

courses.title: Case Management and Substance Abuse
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the process for interviewing substance abuse clients. Includes intake, assessment, handling denial, and ending the interview. Teaches skills for writing short-term goals and treatment plans with emphasis on accountability. Examines various reporting devices.

courses.title: Counseling Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies major counseling theories, their contributions and limitations, and the application of each to a counseling interaction. Students develop their own personal counseling theory.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Hotel-Restaurant Organization and Management II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history, opportunities, problems and trends of the hospitality industry. Covers the organization of the various sectors of the hospitality industry including human resources, general business considerations, and management theory. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: The Art of Garnishing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the relationship between colors and shapes and how they pertain to garnishes. Provides student with knowledge to create impressive presentations.

courses.title: Commercial Food Production Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches commercial cooking. Studies management's role in setting up and running commercial cooking operations, menu planning, menu evaluation, standardization of recipes, and scheduling of manpower.

courses.title: Food Purchasing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the method and procedures for purchasing food for hotels, restaurants and institutions. Deals with markets, federal and trade grades, governmental regulations, packaging, comparative versions price buying, yields and quality control.

courses.title: Principles of Event Planning and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the detailed aspects of how to produce, stage, script, and manage special events within the context of achieving organizational goals. Emphasizes the five critical stages in planning and managing successful special events: research needs and make goal assessments; design events to meet organizational purposes; planning the effective event; coordination and on-site management; and post-event evaluation.

courses.title: Principles and Applications of Catering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Analyzes and compares the principles of on-premise and off- premise catering. Includes student presentations in a series of catered functions where they assume typical managerial/employee positions emphasizing planning, organizing, operating, managing and evaluating.

courses.title: Hospitality Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies legal principles governing hospitality operations. Includes applications of common law and statutory decisions, discussion of legal theory, and regulations governing management of hospitality enterprise.

courses.title: Introduction to Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces commercial horticulture industry with emphasis on career opportunities. Examines equipment, facilities, and physical arrangements of production, wholesale and retail establishments. Surveys individual areas within horticulture industry.

courses.title: Plant Propagation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and practices of plant propagation. Examines commercial and home practices. Provides experience in techniques using seed-spores, cuttings, grafting, budding, layering and division.

courses.title: History of Garden Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the development of gardens as they chronicle the development of civilization. Introduces the periods, in both Europe and North America, beginning with settlement, on through industrial development, land and space utilization to current environmental concerns. Explores physical and cultural influences on garden design and utilization.

courses.title: Greenhouse Crop Production I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers commercial practices related to production of floriculture crops. Considers production requirements, environmental control and management, and cultural techniques.

courses.title: Chemicals in Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes basic chemical principles and their application to horticulture. Introduces principles of inorganic and organic chemicals. Studies chemical activities of insecticides, fungicides, herbicides, fertilizers, and growth regulators.

courses.title: Horticultural Botany
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies taxonomy, anatomy, morphology, physiology, and genetics of plants as applied to identification, propagation and culture.

courses.title: Four Season Food Production
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Familiarizes students with organic small-scale food production through lecture and demonstration. Includes seed saving, cover crops, and gardening planning.

courses.title: Training for Commercial Pesticide Application
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles and practices for safe pesticide usage as required by law in the state of Virginia. Prepares students for the official tests administered by VDACS (Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services).

courses.title: Applied Mathematics for the Green Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the basic math skills needed in the Green Industry to include areas, volumes, calibration calculations, profit and loss statements, and topics specific to turf, landscape, greenhouse, nursery, and interior landscapes.

courses.title: Landscape Plants I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies landscape use of plants. Considers ornamental value, growth habit, identification, and limitations. Part I of II.

courses.title: Landscape Plants II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies landscape use of plants. Considers ornamental value, growth habit, identification, and limitations. Part II of II.

courses.title: Soils
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theoretical and practical aspects of soils and other growing media. Examines media components, chemical and physical properties, and soil organisms. Discusses management and conservation.

courses.title: Plant Pest Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of plant pest management. Covers morphology and life cycles of insects and other small animal pests and plant pathogens. Lab stresses diagnosis, chemical and non-chemical control of specific pests, and pesticide safety.

courses.title: Site Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines basic landscape and site planning techniques, environmental considerations and construction principles.

courses.title: Planting Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies landscape theory and principles of drawing to the planning of residential and small scale commercial landscape designs.

courses.title: Planting Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies landscape theory and principles of drawing to the planning of large scale landscape designs.

courses.title: Landscape Drawing Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies theories of landscape design and drawing to actual design projects and tasks. Emphasizes drawing techniques and use of advanced media in applications. Includes hard line, free-style, and computer-assisted landscape drawing in simple landscape drawing applications.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting and Design (CADD) for Landscape Designers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: HRT 231 . Pre or Co-requisite: HRT 232 .
courses.description: Provides instruction in the use of computer-aided drafting and design software for developing landscape plans and supporting information for drawings such as dimension and area calculations.

courses.title: Woody Plants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies identification, culture, and uses of woody plants in landscaping. Includes deciduous and evergreen, native and cultivated shrubs, trees and vines. Teaches scientific and common names of plants.

courses.title: Herbaceous Plants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies identification, culture and uses of herbaceous plants in landscaping. Includes perennials, biennials, common bulbs and annuals. Teaches scientific and common names of plants.

courses.title: Indoor Plants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies identification, culture, and uses of indoor plants in interior landscaping. Includes tropical, subtropical and non-hardy temperate plants. Teaches scientific and common names of plants.

courses.title: Plant Composition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisites: HRT 245 or HRT 201 .
courses.description: Applies basic knowledge of identification and landscape traits of woody landscape plants from the prerequisite base. Emphasizes plant groupings/combinations to create baselines, focalization, urban/suburban tree use, foundation groupings and screening.

courses.title: Arboriculture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the techniques of tree care. Covers surgery, pruning, insect and disease recognition and control, fertilization, cabling, and lightning rod installation.

courses.title: Introduction to Floral Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for the composition of basic table arrangements. Includes the history of design styles, identification of flowers and green, identification and use of equipment, and conditioning and handling of flowers.

courses.title: Professional Turf Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers turf grass identification selection, culture, propagation, and pest control. Surveys commercial turf care operations and use of common equipment.

courses.title: Landscape Construction and Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines practical applications of commercial landscape construction techniques, and materials used. Covers construction, planting, and maintenance.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Early Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from prehistory up to the 1300s, integrating the arts, literature, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Modern Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from the 1300s until 1900s, integrating the visual arts, literature, religion, music and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Women and Gender Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Broadens understanding and awareness of women by exploring different cultural, historical, and gendered experiences of social groups throughout the world in relationship to such fields as art, literature, religion, philosophy, social sciences, and music. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to African American Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an interdisciplinary approach to the study of African-American life, history, and culture. Examines specific events, ideologies, and individuals that have shaped the contours of African-American life. Studies the history, sociology, economics, religion, politics, psychology, creative productions, and culture of African- Americans. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Comparative Mythology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the cultural expressions of mythology. Considers selected mythologies representing diverse global culture, with emphasis on parallels and divergences in structure, purpose, and representation in literature and the arts. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: The Greek and Roman Tradition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the significance of Greek and Roman cultures on the individual and society, expressed prominently from the Classical Age in Athens to its survival during Roman times. Examines the key contributions that the Greeks and Romans have imparted upon storytelling, theater, philosophy, civics, political morphology, and the arts and the impact they have in the modern world. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Theory and Techniques of Interior Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces drafting and presentation, color theory, and coordination, space planning and arrangement of furnishings.

courses.title: Architectural Drafting for Interior Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces tools and equipment, lettering, methods of construction, designing and delineation of architecture.

courses.title: Three Dimensional Drawing and Rendering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in graphic presentation of three- dimensionally drawn interiors. Presents the use of colored media to render three-dimensional drawings.

courses.title: Styles of Furniture and Interiors
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches history of furnishings and interiors from the ancient world to the present.

courses.title: Introduction to Kitchen and Bath Design Systems
courses.contact_hours: 3 credits. 3 lecture hours. 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces quality kitchen and bath design elements in accordance with recognized industry standards. Presents basic components of kitchen and bath design, including assessment of existing conditions and construction systems, measurement, product selection, specification, and communication of the design. Teaches coordination of kitchen and bath design with existing structural, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and ventilation systems.

courses.title: Materials and Sources
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents textiles, floor and wall coverings, and window treatments. Emphasizes construction, fiber, finish, and code applications. May use research and field trips to trade sources representing these elements.

courses.title: Lighting Design for Interiors
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in lighting terminology including sources of light, lamp types, fixture types and controls. Explores lighting design using layering techniques and lighting calculations that are used to determine lighting needs for a variety of spaces.

courses.title: Theory and Research in Commercial Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches graphic standards and specifications in interior design. Explains best practices of accessibility and code compliance for commercial applications. Focuses on program analysis and effective space planning.

courses.title: Designing Commercial Interiors I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents problems in designing and developing presentations with emphasis on retail spaces.

courses.title: Business Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the preparation of documents related to the business of design including contracts, purchase orders, and specifications. Covers business formats, legal issues, and ethics related to interior design as well as interviewing techniques and a discussion of portfolio requirements.

courses.title: Antiques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Involves process of research, authentication, and determining provenance. Covers examples of furnishings, fixtures, textiles, glass, and ceramics. May provide field trips, lectures, examination, and discussion to assist in determining age, condition, and other properties.

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting for Interior Designers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs in the use of computer aided drawing software for drafting of floor plans, elevations, perspectives, and other drawings used to convey design ideas.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Aided Drafting and Design for Interior Designers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces advanced methods of designing project spaces using BIM (Building Information Modeling) software. Includes the development of rendered three dimensional drawings with specialized light settings, entourage, and photo-realistic images.

courses.title: Portfolio and Resume Preparation for Interior Designers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total Contact 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the proper elements of a professional resume for employment in the field. Focuses on the organization of portfolio content and introduces various methods of digital portfolio production as well as traditional formats. Includes detailed instruction on proper oral presentation skills, interview preparation and techniques, and professional attire and behavior.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Introduction to Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour, Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Covers basic Lean and Six Sigma concepts. Examines the importance of Lean and Six Sigma as pertaining to the world of manufacturing. Provides students with the opportunity to demonstrate the impact of Lean and Six Sigma manufacturing environment.

courses.title: Team Concepts & Problem Solving
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies team concepts and problem solving techniques to assist project teams in improving quality and productivity. Provides knowledge of how to work as a team, plan and conduct good meetings, manage logistics and details, gather useful data, communicate the results and implement changes.

courses.title: Instrumentation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-4 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the fundamental scientific principles of process control including temperature, pressure, level, and flow measurements. Topics include transducers, thermometers, and gauges are introduced along with calibration.

courses.title: Process Control Integration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-4 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week. Prerequisites: INS 230 and ELE 233 .
courses.description: Presents computer automation including PLCs, SCADA, and PC-based systems to control processes. Topics such as PLC control and computer data acquisition are introduced where students will use existing systems or build systems and control these systems with PLCs and computer data acquisition systems. Assesses students through test and project evaluations and the course will be assessed by graduate feedback.

courses.title: Interpreting Foundations I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops fundamental skills of interpreting, including cognitive processes and intralingual language development in English and ASL. Reviews Process Models of interpreting, and uses one to analyze interpretations. Develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process. Part I of II.

courses.title: Interpreting Foundations I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops fundamental skills of interpreting, including cognitive processes and intralingual language development in English and ASL. Reviews Process Models of interpreting, and uses one to analyze interpretations. Develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process. Part II of II.

courses.title: Translation Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 105 .
courses.description: Further develops fundamental skills needed for the task of interpreting Targets comprehending source language (either ASL or English), transferring content into memory store (breaking from original form), restructuring into target language, maintaining message equivalence, conveying implicit and inferred information, and applying appropriate discourse structure. Review Process Model of interpreting, and uses it to analyze translations. Further develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process.

courses.title: Interpreting: An Introduction to the Profession
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic principles and practices of interpreting, focusing on the history of the profession, logistics of interpreting situations, regulatory and legislative issues, resources, and the Code of Ethics. Describes the state quality assurance screening and national certification exam systems, including test procedures.

courses.title: ASL-to-English Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Begins consecutively interpreting monologues from the source language (ASL) to the target language (English). Watch entire ASL monologues process them, analyze them, then choose appropriate English to match the message. Eventually interpret the monologue into English. Puts interpreting theory into practice in a lab environment. Conducts research in the field of interpretation. Develops team interpreting techniques. Interacts with consumers of ASL-English interpretation.

courses.title: English-to-ASL Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Begins consecutively interpreting monologues from the source language (English) to the target language (ASL). Listen to entire English monologues, process them, analyze them, then choose appropriate ASL to match the message. Puts interpreting theory into practice in a lab environment. Conducts research into the field of interpretation. Develops team interpreting techniques. Encourages interaction with consumers of ASL-English interpretation.

courses.title: Transliterating I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Studies the skills required to transmit spoken English into a manual code for English or an interpreting product with more obvious English influences, and vice versa. Introduces a variety of manual codes and their relationship to American Sign Language and Contact Signing.

courses.title: ASL Discourse Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture Hours: 3, Total Contact Hours: 3
courses.description: Introduces to the study of language and communication between Deaf and hearing clients. Focuses on the features of language use and their impact on communication success in American Sign Language and spoken English.

courses.title: ASL-to English Interpretation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 133 and INT 134 .
courses.description: Perform simultaneous interpretations of monologues in the source language (ASL) to the target language (English). Process an incoming ASL monologue while simultaneously producing an appropriate interpretation in English. Conduct research in the field of interpretation. Apply team interpreting techniques. Interact with consumers of interpretation.

courses.title: English-to-ASL Interpretation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 133 and INT 134 .
courses.description: Perform simultaneous interpretations of monologues in the source language (English) into the target language (ASL). Process an incoming English monologue while simultaneously producing an appropriate interpretation in ASL. Conduct research in the field of interpretation. Apply tem interpreting techniques. Interact with consumers of interpretation.

courses.title: Interpreting ASL in Safe Settings
courses.contact_hours: 2-3 Credits, Lecture 2-3 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 133 and INT 134
courses.description: Studies roles, responsibilities, and experiences involved in interpreting American Sign Language (ASL) in community and educational settings, including ethical and business practices. Analyzes the specific linguistic needs of the clients, managing the environment, and resolving ethical concerns for interpreters.

courses.title: Dialogic Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 233 and INT 234 .
courses.description: Apply interpreting fundamentals. Interpret dialogs between spoken English and ASL users. Analyze interpretations by using a Process Model of Interpreting. Conduct research. Practice team interpreting skills in an interactive interpreting environment. Prepare for the interactive nature of standard interpreting evaluations.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Web Page Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Stresses a working knowledge of web site designs, construction, and management using HTML or XHTML. Includes headings, lists, links, images, image maps, tables, forms, and frames.

courses.title: Structured Query Language
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates a working introduction to commands, functions and operators used in SQL for extracting data from standard databases.

courses.title: PL/SQL Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a working introduction to PL/SQL programming with the Oracle RDBMS environment. Includes PL/SQL fundamentals of block program structure, variables, cursors and exceptions, and creation of program units of procedures, functions, triggers and packages.

courses.title: Machine Learning I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to artificial intelligence and machine learning. Examines basic theory, algorithms, and applications. Focuses on feature engineering and machine learning applications within the larger world of artificial intelligence. Part I of II.

courses.title: Applied Data Science Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews the fundamentals of descriptive and inferential statistics, probability, and distributions, as well as basic dataset manipulation and plotting techniques. Focuses on application to real datasets using graphical user interface (GUI) software tools as well as Python.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Web Page Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates advanced techniques in web site planning, design, usability, accessibility, advanced site management, and maintenance utilizing web editor software(s).

courses.title: Machine Learning II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITD 140 or division approval.
courses.description: Examines theory, algorithms, applications, and issues within the subfield of pattern recognition and machine learning, including feature engineering and extraction, supervised and unsupervised learning. Focuses on theory and practice, with coverage of underlying mathematical and heuristic concepts. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Data Science Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITD 145 or division approval.
courses.description: Surveys Big Data and data analytics, including demonstrations and applications of widely used tools and methods. Offers practice in data extraction and visualization.

courses.title: Advanced Database Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses in-depth instruction in the handling of critical tasks of planning and implementing large databases. Includes an introduction to concepts of advanced data warehousing and database configuration.

courses.title: Data Modeling and Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Oracle or SQL programming including DDL, DML, transaction control & queries with SELECT statement and some exposure to procedural language programming.
courses.description: Introduces life cycle application development methodologies in a systematic approach to developing relational databases and designing applications. Presents content introducing functional and business process modeling, using modeling information to produce application designs, analyzing data requirements as entities, attributes, and relationships and map an entity relationship diagram to an initial database design. Identifies the available automated development tools and utilizes Oracle Developer software to perform practical applications of these concepts.

courses.title: Introduction to Information Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of computers and computing and topics which include impact of computers on society, ethical issues, and terminology. Provides discussion about available hardware and software as well as their application.

courses.title: Spreadsheeting for Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a working knowledge of a commercial spreadsheet package to include design and development of a variety of worksheets, preparing graphs, working with database queries, macro writing, menu techniques, and decision analysis tools.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital and Information Literacy and Computer Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops understanding of digital and information literacy. Introduces basic computer concepts in hardware, software, cyber, cloud, database, and operating systems. Includes hands-on experience developing word processing, spreadsheet and presentation documents. Evaluates the reliability of sources. Covers creating a simple web page. Examines topics such as social, legal, and ethical issues. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Multimedia Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores technical fundamentals of creating multimedia projects with related hardware and software. Students will learn to manage resources required for multimedia production and evaluation and techniques for selection of graphics and multimedia software.

courses.title: Help Desk Support Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes instruction in customer support techniques required for analyzing and coordinating software and hardware solutions for end-user needs. includes evaluation and communication techniques required to provide help desk support necessary to transfer knowledge and enable implementation of a solution.

courses.title: PC Hardware and OS Architecture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers instruction about processors, internal functions, peripheral devices, computer organization, memory management, architecture, instruction format, and basic OS architecture.

courses.title: Advanced Multimedia Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITE 170 .
courses.description: Refines multimedia skills, focusing on project development using digital media; video clips, still images, and audio (sounds, music, and narration).

courses.title: Introduction to Telecommunications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys data transmission systems, communication lines, data sets, network, modes of transmission, protocols, and interfacing. Emphasizes network structure and operation.

courses.title: Introduction to Network Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in networking media, physical and logical topologies, common networking standards and popular networking protocols. Emphasizes the TCP/IP protocol suite and related IP addressing schemes, including CIDR. Includes selected topics in network implementation, support and LAN/WAN connectivity.

courses.title: Microcomputer Operating Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of operating system utilities and multiple-level directory structures, creation of batch files, and configuration of microcomputer environments. May include a study of graphical user interfaces.

courses.title: Personal Computer Hardware and Troubleshooting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes specially designed instruction to give a student a basic knowledge of hardware and software configurations. Includes the installation of various peripheral devices as well as basic system hardware components.

courses.title: Introduction to Networks - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the fundamentals of networking environments, the basics of router operations, and basic router and switch configuration.

courses.title: Switching, Routing and Wireless Essentials - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 154
courses.description: Provides the skills and knowledge to install, operate, and troubleshoot routers and switches in small networks. Introduces students to wireless local area networks (WLANS) and network security concepts.

courses.title: Enterprise Networking, Security, and Automation - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 155
courses.description: Teaches students to configure, troubleshoot, and secure enterprise networks. Introduces students to virtualization, application programming interfaces (APIs) and the configuration management tools that make network automation possible.

courses.title: WAN Technologies - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Concentrates on an introduction to Wide Area Networking (WANs). Includes WAN design, LAPB, Frame Relay, ISDN, HDLC, and PPP.

courses.title: Linux System Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses instruction on the installation, configuration and administration of the Linux operating system and emphasizes the use of Linux as a network client and workstation.

courses.title: Unix 1
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to UNIX operating systems. Teaches login procedures, file creation, UNIX file structure, input/output control, and the UNIX shell.

courses.title: Administration of Network Resources
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the management of local area network servers. Teaches proper structuring of security systems. Explains print queues, disk management, and other local area network (LAN) issues. Presents concerns and issues for the purchase and installation of hardware and software upgrades. Can be taught using any network operating system or a range of operating systems as a delivery tool.

courses.title: Information Storage and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced storage systems, protocol, and architectures including Storage Area Networks (SAN), Network Attached Storage (NAS), Fibre Channel Networks, Internet Protocol SANs (IPSAN), iSCSI, and Content Addressable Storage (CAS).

courses.title: Virtual Infrastructure: Installation and Configuration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores concepts and capabilities of virtual architecture with a focus on the installation, configuration, and management of a virtual infrastructure, and Virtual Center. Covers fundamentals of virtual network design and implementation, fundamentals of storage area networks, virtual switching, virtual system management, and engineering for high availability.

courses.title: Cloud Computing: Infrastructure and Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on cloud infrastructure, deployment, security models, and the key considerations in migrating to cloud computing. Covers the technologies and processes required to build traditional, virtualized, and cloud data center environments, including computation, storage, networking, desktop and application virtualization, business continuity, security, and management.

courses.title: Network Security Basics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the basics of network security in depth. Includes security objectives, security architecture, security models and security layers; risk management, network security policy, and security training. Includes the five security keys, confidentiality integrity, availability, accountability and auditability.

courses.title: Network Attacks, Computer Crime and Hacking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Encompasses in-depth exploration of various methods for attacking and defending a network. Explores network security concepts from the viewpoint hackers and their attack methodologies. Includes topics about hackers, attacks, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) malicious code, computer crime and industrial espionage.

courses.title: Network Communication, Security and Authentication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers an in-depth exploration of various communication protocols with a concentration on TCP/IP. Explores communication protocols from the point of view of the hacker in order to highlight protocol weaknesses. Includes Internet architecture, routing, addressing, topology, fragmentation and protocol analysis, and the use of various utilities to explore TCP/IP.

courses.title: Internet/Intranet Firewalls and E-Commerce Security
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Gives an in-depth exploration of firewall, Web security, and e-commerce security. Explores firewall concepts, types, topology and the firewall's relationship to the TCP/IP protocol. Includes client/server architecture, the Web server, HTML and HTTP in relation to Web Security, and digital certification, D.509, and public key infrastructure (PKI).

courses.title: Introduction to Malware Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 261
courses.description: Provides instruction in fundamentals of malware analysis using open-source tools. Emphasizes malware detection as well as the utilization of industry standard tools to analyze malwares using both static and dynamic techniques.

courses.title: Network Security Layers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth exploration of various security layers needed to protect the network. Explores Network Security from the viewpoint of the environment in which the network operates and the necessity to secure that environment to lower the security risk to the network. Includes physical security, personnel security, operating system security, software security and database security.

courses.title: Legal Topics in Network Security
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours hours per week.
courses.description: Conveys an in-depth exploration of the civil and common law issues that apply to network security. Explores statutes, jurisdictional, and constitutional issues related to computer crimes and privacy. Includes rules of evidence, seizure and evidence handling, court presentation and computer privacy in the digital age.

courses.title: Computer Forensics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 106 , ITN 107 . Co-requisite: ITN 260 .
courses.description: Teaches computer forensic investigation techniques for collecting computer-related evidence at the physical layer from a variety of digital media (hard drives, compact flash and PDAs) and performing analysis at the file system layer. Credit will be given to ITN 275 or ITN 276 and ITN 277 , but not all three courses.

courses.title: Computer Forensics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 276 .
courses.description: Develops skills in the forensic extraction of computer evidence at a logical level using a variety of operating systems and applications (i.e., e-mail) and learn techniques for recovering data from virtual memory, temporary Internet files, and intentionally hidden files. Credit will be given to ITN 275 or ITN 276 and ITN 277 , but not all three courses.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Software Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles and practices of software development. Includes instruction in critical thinking, problem solving skills, and essential programming logic in structured and object-oriented design using contemporary tools.

courses.title: Java Programming I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Entails instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Java. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of console and graphical user interface applications.

courses.title: C++ Programming I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Centers instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming and design using C++. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of C++ applications.

courses.title: Programming IOS Devices
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. 3-4 credits.
courses.description: Examines object-oriented Objective C design and programming concepts for Mac OS X, iPhone and iPad. Introduces the tools and APIs for the latest iOS SDK, and how they fit together to build full-featured iOS and Mac OS X applications.

courses.title: Client Side Scripting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in fundamentals of Internet application design, development, and deployment using client side scripting language(s).

courses.title: Python Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Entails instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Python. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of Python applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Game Design & Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces object-oriented game design and development. Provides overview of the electronic game design and development process and underlines the historical contest, content creation strategies, game careers, and future trends in the industry. Utilizes a game language environment to introduce game design, object-oriented paradigms, software design, software development and product testing. Teaches skills of writing a game design document and creating a game with several levels and objects. Integrate 2D animations, 3D models, sound effects, and background music as well as graphic backgrounds.

courses.title: Gaming and Simulation
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts and applications of gaming and simulation through the use of gaming and simulation tools, as well as through basic programming skills.

courses.title: Project Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concepts of project management as defined by the Project Management Institute, the accreditation body for project management.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Java Programming II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Imparts instruction in application of advanced object-oriented techniques to application development using Java. Emphasizes database connectivity, inner classes, collection classes, networking, and threads.

courses.title: Web Scripting Languages
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisites: ITD 110 , ITP 100 .
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles, systems, and tools used to implement Web applications. Provides students with a comprehensive introduction to the programming tools and skills required to build and maintain interactive Web sites. Students will develop Web applications utilizing client-side and server-side scripting languages along with auxiliary tools needed for complete applications.

courses.title: Mobile Java Android Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. 3-4 credits.
courses.description: Provides the necessary design and programming skills required for developing applications on mobile devices (smartphones, tablets, etc.). Utilize the Java-based Android Development Kit to create Android applications, from concept to business model to final product.

courses.title: Advanced Android Application Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITP 266 or Instructor Permission
courses.description: Focuses on the development of the advanced Android app. Surveys tools, technologies, principles, and patterns that underpin all Android app development. Emphasizes communication protocols in the Android Platform and secure coding practices of mobile app development.

courses.title: C++ Programming II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents in-depth instruction of advanced object-oriented techniques for data structures using C++.

courses.title: Advanced Python Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITP 150
courses.description: object-oriented design and advanced programming concepts using Python through instruction and hands-on programming. Emphasizes Object-oriented design (OOD) Object Orient Programming (OOP) concepts, such as classes, inheritance, polymorphism, Object-oriented design patterns, and Unified Modeling Language (UML). Examines best practices, code reusability, and exploration of Python modules and advanced topics.

courses.title: Programming for Cybersecurity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITP 100 , Software Design
courses.description: Teaches scripting techniques for automating security tasks such as network monitoring and penetration testing using a high-level programming language common to cybersecurity professionals. Includes how to write custom tools and the basics of developing software exploits.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Beginning Japanese I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Japanese II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: JPN 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Japanese, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Japanese I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: JPN 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school Japanese, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Japanese II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: JPN 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school Japanese, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Latin I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Latin II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total hours 4 per week. Prerequisite: LAT 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Latin, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Latin I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: LAT 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school Latin, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Latin II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: LAT 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school Latin, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to the Law and the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various areas of law in which a paralegal may be employed. Includes study of the court system (Virginia and federal); a brief overview of criminal law, torts, family law, evidence, the U.C.C., contracts, and ethics; the role of the paralegal; and other areas of interest.

courses.title: Real Estate Law for Legal Assistants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies law of real property and gives in-depth survey of the more common types of real estate transactions and conveyances such as deeds, contracts, leases, and deeds of trust. Focuses on drafting these various instruments and studies the system of recording and search of public documents.

courses.title: Family Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies elements of a valid marriage, grounds for divorce and annulment, separation, defenses, custody, support, adoptions, and applicable tax consequences. Includes property settlement agreements, pre- and ante-nuptial agreements, pleadings, and rules of procedure. May include specific federal and Virginia consumer laws.

courses.title: Legal Research
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of various components of a law library, and emphasizes research skills through the use of digests, encyclopedias, reporter systems, codes, citations, ALR, and other research tools. May include research through electronic databases, overview of computer applications, and writing projects.

courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Studies proper preparation of various legal documents, including legal memoranda, letters, and pleadings. Involves practical applications. May include case and appellate briefs.

courses.title: Ethics for the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hour per week.
courses.description: Examines general principles of ethical conduct applicable to paralegals. Includes the application of rules of ethics to the practicing paralegal.

courses.title: Torts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of the law of torts and may include preparation and use of pleadings and other documents involved in the trial of a civil action. Emphasizes intentional torts, negligence, personal injury, products liability, and malpractice cases.

courses.title: Trial Practice and the Law of Evidence
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces civil and criminal evidence, including kinds, degrees and admissibility of evidence. Studies methods and techniques of evidence acquisition. Emphasizes Virginia and federal rules of evidence. Focuses on the elements and various problems associated with the trial of a civil or criminal case.

courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on major crimes, including their classification, elements of proof, intent, conspiracy, responsibility, parties, and defenses. Emphasizes Virginia law. May include general principles of applicable constitutional law and criminal procedure.

courses.title: Estate Planning and Probate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various devices used to plan an estate, including wills, trust, joint ownership and insurance. Considers various plans in light of family situations and estate objectives. Focuses on practices involving administration of an estate including taxes and preparation of forms.

courses.title: Legal Transactions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an in-depth study of general contract law, including formation, breach, enforcement, and remedies. May include an overview of UCC sales, commercial paper, and collections.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Business Organizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of agency law and the formation of business organizations. Includes sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporation, limited liability companies, and other business entities. Reviews preparation of the documents necessary for the organization and operation of businesses.

courses.title: Immigration Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to immigration law and policy, giving an overview of the United States legal system that regulates the admission, exclusion, removal, and naturalization of immigrants. Includes issues concerning refugees, asylum seekers, illegal immigrants, and undocumented aliens.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Introduction to Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in arithmetic through introduction to variables and equations.

courses.title: Learning Support for Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 154
